races.title: State Senate, District 35
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Todd Johnson
cands.bio: Republican state senator for North Carolina Senate District 35 (Cabarrus and Union counties) since January 2019. Insurance agent and UNC-Chapel Hill graduate (2000). Former Union County commissioner. Sought the 2016 Republican nomination for U.S. House District 9. Has served on the Jesse Helms Center board.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Todd Johnson was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. We found no documented actions in office, such as sponsored bills, tied to the issues we track, and no public statements from him on data centers, development, homestead taxes, or school choice. His only stated positions come from a 2016 congressional campaign website quoted on Ballotpedia, and he has not filled out Ballotpedia's candidate surveys. No endorsements or controversies turned up in the pages we reviewed. The details of his time as a Union County commissioner could not be confirmed beyond one short mention.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the North Carolina Senate since 2019 (Finance, Commerce and Insurance, and Agriculture/Natural and Economic Resources appropriations work). Former Union County commissioner. Works as an insurance agent.
qual.why: Long state legislative service plus earlier local elected office and a business career in insurance fit the high band for a job that writes law and the state budget. Committee chairmanships and his nonprofit board seat were not counted. The Union County commissioner detail comes from a short Wikipedia entry and is not confirmed elsewhere.
qual.label: Long state legislative service plus earlier local elected office and a business career in insurance fit the high band for a job that writes law and the state budget. Committee chairmanships and his nonprofit board seat were not counted. The Union County commissioner detail comes from a short Wikipedia entry and is not confirmed elsewhere.

second-amendment.evidence: His 2016 U.S. House campaign website said gun ownership is an American birthright and called the Second Amendment "America's First Freedom." This was a congressional campaign, not a state Senate one.

pro-life.evidence: His 2016 U.S. House campaign website said he is "100% Pro-Life" and would promote alternatives to abortion in public policy.

workers-first.evidence: His 2016 U.S. House campaign website said "illegal means illegal" and favored immigration reform to "restore the rule of law." It did not mention H-1B visas or state-level enforcement.

cands.name: Christine E. Winward
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 35 in 2026. She advanced from an uncontested primary and lost the general election to incumbent Todd Johnson (R). No other biographical details were found.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as recommended in four Sway voter-guide groups: Readers Picking Leaders, Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress, Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy, and Waves of Democracy. These are voter-guide groups, not organizations that made formal endorsements.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Christine Winward was born or raised, when she moved to North Carolina, or her job history. She has held no prior elected office that we could confirm. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and we found no campaign site, interviews or questionnaires. We therefore could not document her positions on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, campaign money, policing, guns, abortion or schools, and found no public stance on data centers or development. We found no controversies or foreign ties, but the sources were very thin.

qual.background: No occupation, work history or prior office could be verified from the available page.
qual.why: Her background could not be found, so no score was given.
